page_meta.description: Flu treatment online for California adults. Board-certified Family Medicine MD. Antiviral prescriptions (oseltamivir). Self pay $49. Aetna in-network. Same-day video visits. CA telehealth compliant.

california_epidemiology.summary: California reported some of the highest influenza activity levels in the nation during recent seasons. The California Department of Public Health reports that flu causes an estimated 5–20% of the U.S. population to fall ill each year; in California, this translates to approximately 2–8 million illness episodes annually, with 140,000–810,000 hospitalizations nationwide per CDC estimates.

clinical_content.specialty_authority: CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) and IDSA
telehealth_appropriate_criteria: Adult 18+ located in California at time of visit
Sudden onset fever, body aches, fatigue, headache, or cough consistent with flu
Symptom onset within the past 48 hours (antiviral window)
No difficulty breathing, chest pain, or confusion
Seeking antiviral prescription (oseltamivir/Tamiflu or baloxavir/Xofluza) to shorten illness duration
red_flags_requiring_in_person: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Persistent confusion or altered mental status
Severe vomiting that prevents keeping fluids down
Signs of dehydration: no urination for 8+ hours, very dark urine, dizziness
Fever above 104°F (40°C) that does not respond to antipyretics
Symptoms improve then return with worsening fever and cough

drug_pricing.source_note: GoodRx prices are national averages. Prices represent GoodRx coupon price as of May 2026.

medications.name: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) 75 mg
medications.notes: First-line antiviral per CDC. Most effective when started within 48 hours of symptom onset. Generic widely available.

medications.name: Baloxavir marboxil (Xofluza) 40 mg or 80 mg
medications.typical_regimen: Single dose (40 mg if <80 kg; 80 mg if ≥80 kg)
medications.notes: Single-dose oral antiviral per CDC 2025–2026 guidance. Alternative to oseltamivir. Do not use with antacids within 2 hours.

medications.name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) — OTC
medications.typical_regimen: 325–650 mg every 4–6 hours as needed; max 3,000 mg/day
medications.notes: For fever and body ache symptom relief. Do not exceed recommended dose. Avoid if significant liver disease.

faqs.question: Can I get flu treatment online in California?
faqs.answer: Yes. California Business and Professions Code Section 2290.5 permits California-licensed physicians to deliver care via synchronous video telehealth without a prior in-person visit. TeleDirectMD physicians are licensed in California. Adults 18+ in California can book a same-day video visit. If your symptom onset is within 48 hours and you have classic flu symptoms without red flags, a physician may prescribe an antiviral such as oseltamivir (Tamiflu) or baloxavir (Xofluza). Self pay is $49; Aetna is in-network as of April 30, 2026.

faqs.question: Is there a time window for antiviral flu medication to work?
faqs.answer: Yes. Per CDC and IDSA 2025–2026 guidance, antiviral medications — oseltamivir (Tamiflu) and baloxavir (Xofluza) — are most effective when started within 48 hours of symptom onset. They reduce illness duration by approximately 1–2 days and reduce the risk of complications. Antivirals can still be beneficial for high-risk patients (age 65+, immunocompromised, chronic lung or heart disease, pregnancy) even after 48 hours. If you are in a high-risk group, book immediately even if symptoms started 2+ days ago.

faqs.question: How much does oseltamivir (Tamiflu) cost in California?
faqs.answer: Generic oseltamivir is available with a GoodRx coupon for approximately $25–$30 for a 5-day course (10 capsules) at California pharmacies including CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Walmart, and Safeway. Verify current pricing at goodrx.com/oseltamivir before your visit. Prescription costs at the pharmacy are separate from the TeleDirectMD visit fee ($49).

faqs.question: What is the difference between a cold and the flu?
faqs.answer: Influenza typically causes sudden onset of high fever (often above 101°F), severe body aches, headache, and profound fatigue — symptoms that usually come on over hours and feel more debilitating than a cold. The common cold typically causes gradual onset of runny nose, mild sore throat, and nasal congestion without high fever or severe myalgia. While no video visit can definitively distinguish cold from flu without a rapid test, the history and symptom pattern guide clinical decision-making for antiviral prescribing.

faqs.question: Does California require an in-person visit before telehealth?
faqs.answer: No. California B&P Code §2290.5 does not require a prior in-person visit. A California-licensed physician can establish a new patient relationship and evaluate your symptoms through a synchronous video visit. TeleDirectMD documents telehealth consent at the start of every visit.

faqs.question: Is my Aetna plan in California in-network with TeleDirectMD?
faqs.answer: Aetna became an active in-network payor for TeleDirectMD in California effective April 30, 2026. If you hold an Aetna commercial plan in California, you may be able to use your in-network benefits. Always verify current in-network status directly with Aetna before your visit.

faqs.question: Is UnitedHealthcare in-network with TeleDirectMD in California?
faqs.answer: UnitedHealthcare Commercial was approved for California effective May 29, 2026, covering commercial plans and Medicare Advantage. This excludes Medi-Cal, Individual Exchange, and Navigate/Charter/Core plan types. Verify your specific UHC plan eligibility before booking.

faqs.question: When is flu dangerous and when should I go to the ER in California?
faqs.answer: Seek emergency care immediately for difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, confusion, severe vomiting preventing fluid intake, signs of dehydration (no urination for 8+ hours, dizziness), or fever above 104°F not responding to antipyretics. People at high risk for flu complications — adults over 65, immunocompromised, pregnant, or with chronic heart or lung disease — should contact a physician within 24 hours of symptom onset regardless of severity.

faqs.question: Will Medi-Cal cover my TeleDirectMD flu visit in California?
faqs.answer: TeleDirectMD is not currently enrolled as a Medi-Cal provider. If you have Medi-Cal, you can use the $49 self-pay rate, or find a Medi-Cal-enrolled telehealth provider through your managed care plan or the California DHCS directory at dhcs.ca.gov.

faqs.question: Should I get a flu vaccine in California?
faqs.answer: Yes. The California Department of Public Health recommends annual influenza vaccination for all Californians 6 months and older, per CDC ACIP guidance. Vaccination is the most effective prevention strategy — it reduces the risk of flu illness, hospitalization, and death. Even if vaccinated, you may contract flu, but illness is typically less severe. TeleDirectMD can discuss vaccination with you; vaccination itself is available at California pharmacies, community health centers, and primary care offices statewide.

faqs.question: Does California's AB 744 telehealth parity law apply to flu treatment visits?
faqs.answer: California AB 744 (2019) requires commercial health plans to reimburse telehealth services on the same basis as in-person services. Parity applies when the provider is already in-network with your specific plan. Currently, Aetna (active April 30, 2026) and UnitedHealthcare Commercial (active May 29, 2026) are in-network in California for TeleDirectMD.

faqs.question: How quickly will my antiviral prescription reach a California pharmacy?
faqs.answer: California requires all prescriptions to be issued electronically under Assembly Bill 2789 (effective January 1, 2022). If antiviral treatment is appropriate, TeleDirectMD sends an e-prescription electronically to your chosen California pharmacy during or immediately after your visit. Most California pharmacies fill within one to four hours. Starting antivirals quickly matters — the sooner within that 48-hour window, the better.
